trigger_evidence: GitHub Actions run 35164504054 failed in the control-plane job while local full-history validation passed.
The failing command was validate_execution_contracts.py and the exact error was: drift:architecture-control-current implementation_commit is not available in repository history.

The control-plane workflow checkout used actions/checkout without fetch-depth override, so the CI repository was shallow and did not contain the historical implementation commit required by the drift validator.

After the first one-workflow EV2 repair was pushed, GitHub Actions run 35164665169 failed in AI Governance Evals with the same validate_execution_contracts.py historical-commit error, proving the first one-file scope incomplete before EV3.
Both workflows that directly invoke validate_execution_contracts.py therefore require the same full-history checkout contract.

Pre-EV4 review found that the Windows worktree representation of the control-plane workflow had mixed line endings while Git stores the workflow canonically with LF; the EV3 record is therefore repaired to bind committed Git blob bytes so the exact reviewed manifest is portable to GitHub/fresh-clone readback.
hypothesis: Providing full Git history to both existing CI workflows that invoke the unchanged drift validator will let each workflow verify the historical implementation commit instead of failing because the commit object is absent from a shallow clone.
